result:
Here's what I'd do, in priority order. December is your one strong seasonal moment, so most of the effort should go there.

## 1. Gift subscriptions for Christmas (start now, push until about 20 Dec)
This is the biggest winter opportunity.
- Sell **4-week (€72) and 8-week (€144) gift boxes**, paid upfront, with a printed card the buyer can wrap.
- Sell them in the shop, on your site, and by email to current subscribers. Your 140 subscribers are the most likely buyers, since they'll gift to neighbours, parents and friends.
- The recipient has to live within your 3 km zone. Say this clearly at checkout.
- In week 3 of the gift, send the recipient an offer to continue, such as "keep your Saturday box, first month at €16/week." Most of the long-term growth comes from this step.
- Upfront payments also help cash flow in a slow month.

## 2. Subscriber referrals (run all winter)
In a 3 km radius, word of mouth beats paid ads.
- Offer **one free box to the referrer once the new subscriber's 2nd delivery is done**, and a first box at half price for the new subscriber.
- That costs you about €27 in revenue, and less in ingredients, per new subscriber. At €78 a month per subscriber it pays back in under two weeks.
- Put a referral card in every box for 3–4 weeks in a row. One email won't be enough.

## 3. Protect the base over the holidays
26 Dec and 2 Jan are both Saturdays. People will be travelling, and a delivery they don't want turns into a cancellation.
- Email in early December offering an easy **"skip a week"** or a pause of up to 4 weeks.
- Make "pause" the default option on the cancel page.
- Keeping 5 subscribers is worth as much as winning 5 new ones, and it's much cheaper.

## 4. Seasonal add-ons and holiday pre-orders
- Offer one or two festive items, like an enriched loaf or a spiced pastry, as **add-ons to the box** and as **one-off holiday pre-orders** for non-subscribers.
- Every pre-order customer gets a delivery to their door. Put a "try the weekly box" card in each one, since those people already live in your zone.

## 5. January "fresh start" push
- Run a **two-week trial at €15/week** in the first half of January, when people are setting new routines and cutting back on supermarket food.
- Hand out tasting samples in the shop on busy Saturdays, with a QR code to the trial.

## Budget (about €300/month)
- **Printing, about €80:** gift cards, referral cards, flyers.
- **Instagram/Facebook ads, about €120–150:** target only your 3 km radius and promote the gift box in December, then the trial in January.
- **Samples and small extras, the rest.**

Most of the cost is discounts and free boxes, which you only pay once someone subscribes.

## Targets to aim for
Net **+20–30 subscribers by end of January**, meaning new subscribers minus cancellations. That's +€360–540/week. Track it weekly. Also track how many gift recipients go on to subscribe; above 25% would be good.

If you can share your current monthly churn and how most subscribers found you, I can tell you which of these to lean on hardest.
